examples.text: Вообще-то у этой актрисы шестеро детей.
examples.trans: Actually, that actress has six children.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.text: Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: Too much to do.

examples.text: Это слишком трудно.
examples.trans: It's too hard.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.

examples.text: Скажи, с ними всё хорошо?
examples.trans: Tell me, is everything all right with them?

examples.text: Всё хорошо, я сделал как ты сказала.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, I did as you said.

examples.text: Дима, я слишком хорошо знаю твой вкус.
examples.trans: Dima, I know your taste all too well.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Лена, я просто не знал!
examples.trans: Lena, I simply did not know!

examples.text: Не знал, что это ваше блюдо.
examples.trans: I did not know that this was your dish.

examples.text: Дима, я слишком хорошо знаю твой вкус.
examples.trans: Dima, I know your taste all too well.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я пять лет ел твою еду.
examples.trans: I ate your food for five years.

examples.text: Я по запаху твои блюда узнаю.
examples.trans: I will recognize your dishes by their smell.

examples.text: Но твоё шоу — для неудачников.
examples.trans: But your show is for losers.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'taste', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: И только по вкусу выбираю.
examples.trans: And I choose only by taste.

examples.text: Дима, я слишком хорошо знаю твой вкус.
examples.trans: Dima, I know your taste all too well.

examples.text: Вы не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: You are not my type.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('this') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Хозяином этого ресторана являюсь я.
examples.trans: The owner of this restaurant is me.

examples.text: Класс, это вообще очень оригинально!
examples.trans: Awesome, that is really original!

examples.text: Это настоящий мастер нашего телевидения.
examples.trans: He is a true master of our television.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.

examples.text: Я просто заранее с тобой репетирую.
examples.trans: I am just rehearsing with you in advance.

examples.text: А чего мы просто так стоим?
examples.trans: And why are we just standing around?

examples.text: Мне просто приснился странный сон.
examples.trans: I just had a strange dream.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'incredibly'.

examples.text: Это просто невероятно вкусное блюдо!
examples.trans: This is simply an incredibly tasty dish!

examples.text: Тебе сегодня просто невероятно повезло.
examples.trans: Today you were simply incredibly lucky.

examples.text: Это было невероятно вкусно.
examples.trans: It was unbelievably delicious.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'tasty', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Это просто невероятно вкусное блюдо!
examples.trans: This is simply an incredibly tasty dish!

examples.text: Сушки очень вкусные.
examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Какой вкусный чай!
examples.trans: What delicious tea!
